title: Utility Types
description: TypeScript's built-in type transformers — reshape interfaces without rewriting them.

challenges.title: Partial — all fields optional
challenges.whyMatters: Partial is used constantly for update/patch operations — when you only want to change some fields of a config or resource, not replace the whole thing.

choices.label: { host?: string; port?: number; timeout?: number }
{ host: string | undefined; port: number | undefined; timeout: number | undefined }
{ host: string; port: number; timeout: number } (unchanged)
Removes all properties

challenges.title: Pick and Omit
challenges.description:
Given:

  interface Service { id: string; name: string; port: number; secret: string }

Which produces `{ id: string; name: string }`?

  A)  Partial<Service>
  B)  Pick<Service, 'id' | 'name'>
  C)  Omit<Service, 'id' | 'name'>
  D)  Required<Service>
challenges.whyMatters: Omit is used when building public-facing types that exclude sensitive fields (like secrets). Pick is used when you only want a subset for a specific function.
hints: Pick keeps the listed keys, Omit removes them

choices.label: A)  Partial<Service>
B)  Pick<Service, 'id' | 'name'>`
C)  Omit<Service, 'id' | 'name'>
D)  Required<Service>

challenges.title: Record — typed key-value maps
challenges.description:
What does `Record<string, number>` represent?

And what would `Record<'prod' | 'staging' | 'dev', string>` look like?
challenges.whyMatters: Environment-to-URL maps, service-to-port maps, status-to-count maps — Record is how you type dictionaries in production tooling.
hints: Record<K, V> is a shorthand for an object where all keys are K and all values are V

choices.label: An array of [string, number] tuples
{ [key: string]: number } — and { prod: string; staging: string; dev: string }
Map<string, number>
A function from string to number

challenges.title: Apply utility types to a patch function
challenges.description:
Given an interface:

  interface Deployment { id: string; name: string; image: string; replicas: number }

Write a function `patch(current: Deployment, updates: Partial<Omit<Deployment, 'id'>>): Deployment`

It should return a new object that merges the current deployment with the updates (id is never updated).

Also write `toPublic(d: Deployment): Omit<Deployment, 'id'>` that returns the deployment without the id field.
challenges.whyMatters: Patch functions appear in every config management system. Omitting id from updates prevents accidentally overwriting resource identifiers.
hints: For toPublic, destructure to remove id: const { id, ...rest } = d

challenges.title: ReturnType and Parameters
challenges.description:
Given:

  function createServer(host: string, port: number): { host: string; port: number; start: () => void } { ... }

What are these types?

  type A = ReturnType<typeof createServer>
  type B = Parameters<typeof createServer>
challenges.whyMatters: ReturnType and Parameters let you derive types from existing functions without duplicating them — essential when working with third-party libraries that don't export their types.
hints: ReturnType extracts what a function returns, Parameters extracts the argument tuple

choices.label: A = { host: string; port: number; start: () => void }  B = [string, number]
A = void  B = string[]
A = Promise<...>  B = unknown[]
Both are any

challenges.title: Build an env config loader with Record
challenges.description:
Write a function `loadEnv(keys: string[]): Record<string, string>` that reads environment variables.

For each key:
- If the env var exists, include it in the result
- If it doesn't exist, throw an Error: `"Missing required env var: KEY"`

Also write `buildServiceUrls(envs: Record<'API_HOST' | 'DB_HOST' | 'CACHE_HOST', string>): Record<string, string>` that returns:
`{ api: 'http://{API_HOST}', db: 'postgresql://{DB_HOST}', cache: 'redis://{CACHE_HOST}' }`
challenges.whyMatters: Loading and validating env vars at startup is one of the first things any software engineering script does. Typed Records make the shape explicit.
hints: Use reduce or a for loop to build the Record
The envs parameter keys are a union literal — use them directly in the template

challenges.title: Readonly — immutable types
challenges.whyMatters: Marking config objects as Readonly prevents accidental mutation — especially important when the same config object is passed to multiple services.
hints: Readonly makes all properties non-writable at the type level

choices.label: No error — Readonly is only a hint
Cannot assign to 'port' because it is a read-only property
Type 'number' is not assignable to type 'string'
Runtime error only, not compile time

challenges.title: Compose utility types for a real shape
challenges.description:
Given:

  interface ServiceSpec { id: string; name: string; image: string; port: number; secret: string; replicas: number }

Using only utility types (no new interface declarations), derive and export:

- `PublicSpec` — ServiceSpec without id and secret
- `PatchSpec` — all fields of PublicSpec optional
- `EnvMap` — a Record mapping 'prod' | 'staging' | 'dev' to PublicSpec

Then write `makeEnvMap(specs: PublicSpec[]): EnvMap` — takes exactly 3 specs (prod, staging, dev in that order) and returns the EnvMap.
challenges.whyMatters: Deriving types from a single source of truth avoids drift — change ServiceSpec and all derived types update automatically.
hints: makeEnvMap destructures the array: const [prod, staging, dev] = specs
